extracted.intended_audience: general readers; writers and readers interested in Anne Lamott and her approach to writing
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia biography page summarizing Anne Lamott's life, career, major works, and statements about her writing; useful for readers or writers looking for biographical context and high-level statements of her values as an author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired qualities in books (Anne Lamott's statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: I try to write the books I would love to come upon, that are honest, concerned with real lives, human hearts, spiritual transformation, families, secrets, wonder, craziness—and that can make me laugh. When I am reading a book like this, I feel rich and profoundly relieved to be in the presence of someone who will share the truth with me, and throw the lights on a little, and I try to write these kinds of books. Books, for me, are medicine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lamott articulates a set of evaluative qualities she aims for in books: honesty, attention to real lives and human hearts, engagement with spiritual transformation and family/secret/wonder elements, a balance of craziness and humor, truthful illumination. For writers inspired by her, these are target attributes to strive for in tone, content, and emotional effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone/voice: self-deprecating humor and openness
rubrics_metrics.description: Lamott's writings, marked by their self-deprecating humor and openness, cover such subjects as alcoholism, single-motherhood, depression, and Christianity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies voice as a defining criterion: employ candidness and self-deprecation to approach serious or personal topics. The page implies that an open, humorous, and vulnerable voice is central to Lamott's appeal and a model for similar work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonfiction approach: largely autobiographical
rubrics_metrics.description: Her nonfiction works are largely autobiographical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lamott's nonfiction draws heavily on personal experience; for writers following her model, using memoir-like personal material and reflection is a preferred method for authenticity and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequent themes/subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Lamott's writings cover such subjects as alcoholism, single-motherhood, depression, and Christianity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These topics indicate the thematic territory Lamott occupies—difficult personal struggles, family dynamics, mental health, and faith. Writers emulating her approach might foreground similarly intimate, often spiritual or recovery-oriented subject matter.
